claims.explanation: RITA binds p53 and disrupts the p53-MDM2 interaction, reactivating wild-type p53 to induce apoptosis. Selectivity is therefore expected to depend on the presence of functional wild-type p53 and intact downstream apoptotic signaling; TP53-mutant lines are generally less responsive, while wild-type TP53 lines with intact p53 pathway components are more sensitive. Additional modifiers such as MDM2 amplification or high MDM2 expression may reduce free p53 and confer resistance, whereas loss of p53-negative regulators or intact apoptosis effectors may enhance killing.

features.basis: RITA requires wild-type p53 to reactivate; TP53 mutations impair response
High MDM2 can sequester p53 and limit RITA-mediated reactivation
Loss of p16/CDKN2A may impair cell-cycle checkpoints and enhance apoptosis
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT survival signaling but may also increase dependence on p53-mediated apoptosis
PIK3CA mutations are common in sensitive lines and may alter survival signaling
KRAS mutations are enriched in sensitive lines and may create oncogene-induced stress
BRAF mutations are present in several sensitive lines and may sensitize to apoptosis
ARID1A mutations appear in sensitive lines and may affect chromatin remodeling and p53 target accessibility
PMAIP1 (NOXA) is upregulated by RITA in the virtual cell and promotes apoptosis
AURKA is repressed by p53; high AURKA may counteract p53-mediated apoptosis
STAT3 antagonizes p53-mediated repression of survival genes
p53 induction upregulates ULBP1, enhancing NK cell-mediated killing
